newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium asks French for more Dassault papers.
newsitem.headline: Belgium asks French for more Dassault papers.

text.p: Belgium has pressed France to hand over more documents in a continuing probe into allegations that French aerospace group Dassault paid bribes to win a military contract at the end of the 1980s, Belgian newspapers said on Thursday.

Last month a French court finally gave Belgian police some of the papers they had requested more than a year earlier, after Belgian Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck personally contacted his French counterpart Jacques Toubon.

Belgian media said De Clerck had now intervened again, asking the French to surrender the remaining documents relating to a front company which Belgian police believe was used to pay the bribes. The papers were seized by French police in November 1995.
The Belgian justice ministry was not immediately available to comment on the reports.

The police are investigating claims Dassault paid 600 million Belgian francs ($19 million) in kickbacks to Belgian political parties to secure a 1989 contract to fit air defence systems to the country's F-16 fighter jets.

After months of lying dormant the "Dassault affair" has sprung to life in recent weeks and even threatened the stability of Belgium's centre-left coalition government when top francophone Socialist Party (PS) officials were arrested on corruption charges in connection with the investigation.
A former PS accountant has also been arrested.
A Belgian court last year issued an international arrest warrant for Serge Dassault, group founder and chairman, who has denied all wrong doing but has refused to come to Belgium to answer questions.
